title: He led the US government's global development agency. Now he leads a 110-year-old philanthropy. In 2026, TIME named him to its Philanthropy 100.

sources.text: American Bazaar - 3 Indian Americans in 2026 TIME100 Philanthropy list
The Global Indian - Three Indian Americans named to TIME100 Philanthropy 2026 list

caption:
He led the US government's global development agency. Now he leads a 110-year-old philanthropy. In 2026, TIME named him to its Philanthropy 100.

Shah is President of the Rockefeller Foundation - its 13th and the first Indian-American to lead the institution since its founding over a century ago. TIME recognized his work directing the foundation's initiatives on global health, climate resilience, food security and economic opportunity.

Born in Detroit to Gujarati immigrant parents, Shah served as the 16th Administrator of USAID from 2010 to 2015 before taking the Rockefeller Foundation presidency in 2017 - institutional leadership, not a single donation.

Shah's path from a government development agency to one of philanthropy's oldest institutions shows diaspora influence operating at the level of policy and strategy, not just individual gifts.
